candidates.text: The representative ESA (the rear lamp with its LED modules and drive circuitry) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 6 of this Regulation for ESA type approval to be granted; paragraph 7 does not apply because the lamp has no REESS charging-mode function.
candidates.test_case: Check that the ESA test reports cover broadband and narrowband emission, radiated immunity and Annex 10 conducted transients, and that all results pass.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp is approved as an ESA, and approval depends on meeting the paragraph 6 emission and immunity requirements.

candidates.text: In case the LED light source is a non-replaceable LED module, the ESA (part of a light source) shall be accompanied by a test report from a designated Technical Service stating that the ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128; without this report, R10 approval of the ESA shall not be granted.
candidates.test_case: Check that the approval file contains a Technical Service report confirming the LED module is not mechanically interchangeable with R37/R99/R128 light sources.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's ESA is part of a light source (non-replaceable LED modules), so R10 approval depends on this documentation.

candidates.text: In case the LED light source is a replaceable LED light source, the approval number granted to this ESA under Regulation No. 128 (or No. 37 / No. 99) shall be specified; without this documentation, R10 approval of the ESA shall not be granted.
candidates.test_case: Check the application documents for a valid R128 approval number for the LED light source.
candidates.applies_because: This is the alternative light-source option, where the ESA is an approved replaceable LED light source.

candidates.text: An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA (rear lamp) conforming to a type approved under UN R10.
candidates.test_case: Inspect production samples of the rear lamp for the presence of the R10 approval mark.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp with LED modules on PCB is an ESA seeking component/STU approval under R10.

candidates.text: The international approval mark shall be affixed in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form.
candidates.test_case: Compare the mark location on the lamp with the location stated on the approval communication form.
candidates.applies_because: The ESA approval mark must follow the format and placement of paragraph 5.3.

candidates.text: The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for the circled "E" and the correct country number.
candidates.applies_because: Defines the required content of the ESA approval mark on the lamp.

candidates.text: The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation (10), followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, placed to the right of the circle.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for "10R-" followed by the approval number to the right of the circle.
candidates.applies_because: Defines the required content and arrangement of the ESA approval mark on the lamp.

candidates.text: The approval markings on the ESA may be located so that they are not visible when the ESA (rear lamp) is installed in the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Check that the mark is present on the lamp (e.g. on the housing rear side), even if it is hidden after installation.
candidates.applies_because: This permission relaxes mark visibility for the ESA in its installed position on the vehicle.

candidates.text: The ESA (rear combination lamp with LED modules and drive electronics) shall be designed, constructed and fitted so that the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, can comply with the requirements of UN R10.
candidates.test_case: Design review of the lamp's EMC design, followed by completion of all applicable ESA EMC tests.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's LED PCB is an ESA intended for fitting to M1 vehicles.

candidates.text: The ESA shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
candidates.test_case: Check that the test plan and test reports cover radiated emission, conducted transient emission, radiated immunity and conducted transient immunity.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is approved as an ESA, so the full set of ESA emission and immunity tests applies.

candidates.text: The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.
candidates.test_case: Perform an Annex 7 broadband radiated emission measurement on the lamp in normal operation (all lamp functions on).
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is an ESA subject to the broadband emission limits.

candidates.text: When measured according to Annex 7, the ESA broadband radiated emission limit in the 30 to 75 MHz band shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz.
candidates.test_case: Compare Annex 7 quasi-peak readings from 30 to 75 MHz with the log-decreasing limit line of Appendix 6.
candidates.applies_because: The broadband limit applies to the LED drive electronics of the lamp.

candidates.text: When measured according to Annex 7, the ESA broadband radiated emission limit in the 75 to 400 MHz band shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 6).
candidates.test_case: Compare Annex 7 readings from 75 to 400 MHz with the log-increasing limit line of Appendix 6.
candidates.applies_because: The broadband limit applies to the LED drive electronics of the lamp.

candidates.text: When measured according to Annex 7, the ESA broadband radiated emission limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
candidates.test_case: Compare Annex 7 readings from 400 to 1,000 MHz with the 63 dBµV/m limit.
candidates.applies_because: The broadband limit applies to the LED drive electronics of the lamp.

candidates.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type-approval limits.
candidates.test_case: Verify that all broadband readings lie below the limit line across 30 to 1,000 MHz.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion for the lamp's broadband emission test.

candidates.text: The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.
candidates.test_case: Perform an Annex 8 narrowband radiated emission measurement on the lamp in normal operation.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is an ESA subject to the narrowband emission limits, unless the 6.10.1 exception applies.

candidates.text: When measured according to Annex 8, the ESA narrowband radiated emission limit in the 30 to 75 MHz band shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz.
candidates.test_case: Compare Annex 8 average-detector readings from 30 to 75 MHz with the Appendix 7 limit line.
candidates.applies_because: The narrowband limit applies in case the lamp has an active electronic driver (oscillator above 9 kHz).

candidates.text: When measured according to Annex 8, the ESA narrowband radiated emission limit in the 75 to 400 MHz band shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 7).
candidates.test_case: Compare Annex 8 readings from 75 to 400 MHz with the Appendix 7 limit line.
candidates.applies_because: The narrowband limit applies in case the lamp has an active electronic driver (oscillator above 9 kHz).

candidates.text: When measured according to Annex 8, the ESA narrowband radiated emission limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
candidates.test_case: Compare Annex 8 readings from 400 to 1,000 MHz with the 53 dBµV/m limit.
candidates.applies_because: The narrowband limit applies in case the lamp has an active electronic driver (oscillator above 9 kHz).

candidates.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband emission value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type-approval limits.
candidates.test_case: Verify that all narrowband readings lie below the limit line across 30 to 1,000 MHz.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion for the lamp's narrowband emission test.

candidates.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances by the ESA on its 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 7637-2, as described in Annex 10, against the maximum pulse amplitudes of Table 1.
candidates.test_case: Perform an ISO 7637-2 transient emission measurement on the lamp supply line while the functions are switched on and off.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is supplied from the vehicle's 12/24 V system, and its switched LED circuits can generate transients.

candidates.text: For an ESA for vehicles with 12 V systems, the transient conducted emission on the supply lines shall not exceed a positive pulse amplitude of +75 V.
candidates.test_case: Record the maximum positive pulse amplitude per ISO 7637-2 and compare it with +75 V.
candidates.applies_because: Applies in case the lamp is designed for a 12 V supply.

candidates.text: For an ESA for vehicles with 12 V systems, the transient conducted emission on the supply lines shall not exceed a negative pulse amplitude of -100 V.
candidates.test_case: Record the maximum negative pulse amplitude per ISO 7637-2 and compare it with -100 V.
candidates.applies_because: Applies in case the lamp is designed for a 12 V supply.

candidates.text: For an ESA for vehicles with 24 V systems, the transient conducted emission on the supply lines shall not exceed a positive pulse amplitude of +150 V.
candidates.test_case: Record the maximum positive pulse amplitude per ISO 7637-2 and compare it with +150 V.
candidates.applies_because: Applies in case the lamp is designed for a 24 V supply.

candidates.text: For an ESA for vehicles with 24 V systems, the transient conducted emission on the supply lines shall not exceed a negative pulse amplitude of -450 V.
candidates.test_case: Record the maximum negative pulse amplitude per ISO 7637-2 and compare it with -450 V.
candidates.applies_because: Applies in case the lamp is designed for a 24 V supply.

candidates.text: The immunity of the ESA representative of its type to electromagnetic radiation shall be tested by one or more methods chosen from those described in Annex 9 (absorber chamber/ALSE, TEM cell, BCI, stripline, reverberation chamber).
candidates.test_case: Perform a radiated immunity test on the lamp per Annex 9 using the selected method(s).
candidates.applies_because: The lamp contains immunity-related functions (stop lamp and rear position lamp).

candidates.text: If the stripline method is used, the radiated immunity test level shall be 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz band.
candidates.test_case: Stripline test from 20 to 400 MHz at 60 V/m, confirming coverage of at least 90 % of the band.
candidates.applies_because: This is the immunity severity for the lamp ESA when tested by stripline.

candidates.text: If the TEM cell method is used, the radiated immunity test level shall be 75 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 200 MHz band.
candidates.test_case: TEM cell test from 20 to 200 MHz at 75 V/m.
candidates.applies_because: This is the immunity severity for the lamp ESA when tested in a TEM cell.

candidates.text: If the BCI method is used, the immunity test level shall be 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz band.
candidates.test_case: BCI test on the lamp harness from 20 to 400 MHz at 60 mA.
candidates.applies_because: This is the immunity severity for the lamp ESA when tested by bulk current injection.

candidates.text: If the ALSE method is used, the radiated immunity test level shall be 30 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 80 to 2,000 MHz band and 10 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band.
candidates.test_case: ALSE test at 30 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2 to 6 GHz).
candidates.applies_because: This is the immunity severity for the lamp ESA when tested in an absorber-lined chamber.

candidates.text: If the reverberation chamber method is used, the radiated immunity test level shall be 21 V/m in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz band and 7 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band.
candidates.test_case: Reverberation chamber test at 21 V/m (LUF to 2 GHz) and 7 V/m (2 to 6 GHz).
candidates.applies_because: This is the immunity severity for the lamp ESA when tested in a reverberation chamber.

candidates.text: If the stripline method is used, the minimum radiated immunity test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz band shall be 50 V/m.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the stripline field never falls below 50 V/m from 20 to 400 MHz.
candidates.applies_because: This is the minimum immunity severity for the lamp ESA when tested by stripline.

candidates.text: If the TEM cell method is used, the minimum radiated immunity test level over the whole 20 to 200 MHz band shall be 62.5 V/m.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the TEM cell field never falls below 62.5 V/m from 20 to 200 MHz.
candidates.applies_because: This is the minimum immunity severity for the lamp ESA when tested in a TEM cell.

candidates.text: If the BCI method is used, the minimum immunity test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz band shall be 50 mA.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the injected current never falls below 50 mA from 20 to 400 MHz.
candidates.applies_because: This is the minimum immunity severity for the lamp ESA when tested by bulk current injection.

candidates.text: If the ALSE method is used, the minimum radiated immunity test level shall be 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz band and 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the ALSE field is at least 25 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 8 V/m (2 to 6 GHz) at all frequencies.
candidates.applies_because: This is the minimum immunity severity for the lamp ESA when tested in an absorber-lined chamber.

candidates.text: If the reverberation chamber method is used, the minimum radiated immunity test level shall be 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz band and 6 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the reverberation chamber field is at least 18 V/m (LUF to 2 GHz) and 6 V/m (2 to 6 GHz).
candidates.applies_because: This is the minimum immunity severity for the lamp ESA when tested in a reverberation chamber.

candidates.text: During the radiated immunity tests according to Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of the immunity-related functions of the ESA (stop lamp and rear position lamp).
candidates.test_case: Monitor the stop lamp and rear position lamp light output (e.g. camera or photodetector) throughout exposure; no switching off, flicker or change in intensity is allowed.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp and rear position lamp are listed immunity-related functions.

candidates.text: The immunity of the ESA to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b (Annex 10), with the levels of Tables 3a and 3b. The starting profile shall be assessed by the functional status classification of ISO 16750-1, and the pulses by the FPSC of ISO 7637-1.
candidates.test_case: Apply the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 pulses to the lamp supply input and classify the functional behaviour.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is powered from the vehicle's 12/24 V supply lines.

candidates.text: Where the ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started by a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the ESA shall withstand the ISO 16750-2 starting profile at level II (12 V and 24 V systems), 10 pulses. Functional status shall be class B for immunity-related functions that must be operational during engine start, class C for other immunity-related functions, and class D for functions not related to immunity-related functions (e.g. reversing lamp).
candidates.test_case: Apply 10 level II starting-profile pulses per ISO 16750-2 and check the stop and rear position lamp behaviour against class B/C and the reversing lamp against class D.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp for M1 vehicles may be fitted to ICE vehicles with a starter motor, and it includes both immunity-related and other functions.

candidates.text: The ESA shall withstand ISO 7637-2 pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system) for 500 pulses, with FPSC class III for both immunity-related and other functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply 500 pulses 1 at the applicable level and verify FPSC III for all lamp functions.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is connected to the 12/24 V supply lines.

candidates.text: The ESA shall withstand ISO 7637-2 pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems) for 500 pulses, with FPSC class I for immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) and class III for other functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply 500 pulses 2a at +37 V and verify that the stop and rear position lamps are unaffected (class I) and that the reversing lamp meets class III.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is connected to the 12/24 V supply lines and contains immunity-related functions.

candidates.text: The ESA shall withstand ISO 7637-2 pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system) for 10 pulses, with FPSC class II for immunity-related functions and class III for other functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply 10 pulses 2b at the applicable level and verify class II for the stop and rear position lamps and class III for the reversing lamp.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is connected to the 12/24 V supply lines and contains immunity-related functions.

candidates.text: The ESA shall withstand ISO 7637-2 pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system) for 1 h, with FPSC class I for immunity-related functions and class III for other functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply pulse 3a for 1 h at the applicable level and verify class I for the stop and rear position lamps and class III for the reversing lamp.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is connected to the 12/24 V supply lines and contains immunity-related functions.

candidates.text: The ESA shall withstand ISO 7637-2 pulse 3b at +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system) for 1 h, with FPSC class I for immunity-related functions and class III for other functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply pulse 3b for 1 h at the applicable level and verify class I for the stop and rear position lamps and class III for the reversing lamp.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is connected to the 12/24 V supply lines and contains immunity-related functions.

candidates.text: In case the ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz (e.g. passive resistor/linear LED drive), it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2 and Annex 8 (narrowband emission).
candidates.test_case: Review the schematic and bill of materials to confirm there is no oscillator, switching regulator, PWM or microcontroller clock above 9 kHz.
candidates.applies_because: This exception applies under the open option of passive LED drive electronics.

candidates.text: In case the ESA is not switched, contains no switches or does not include an inductive load, it need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
candidates.test_case: Review the circuit design for internal switching elements and inductive loads to justify omitting the ISO 7637-2 emission test.
candidates.applies_because: This relaxation may apply to the lamp, depending on its LED drive circuit design.

candidates.text: Rear lamps (ESAs) approved under UN R10 shall be manufactured so as to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements of paragraph 6 (paragraph 7 does not apply, as the lamp has no REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid).
candidates.test_case: Audit production samples against the approved ESA specification and repeat the paragraph 6 emission and immunity tests on series parts.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's LED/PCB electronics are an ESA approved under R10, and series production must match the approved type.

candidates.text: When a series-production rear lamp (ESA) is verified for conformity, its measured broadband radiated emission levels shall not exceed the ESA broadband reference limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1 by more than 4 dB (60 per cent). These limits are 62 to 52 dBµV/m (30–75 MHz), 52 to 63 dBµV/m (75–400 MHz) and 63 dBµV/m (400–1,000 MHz).
candidates.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emissions of a production sample per Annex 7 and check that the levels are at or below the 6.5.2.1 limits + 4 dB.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's ESA is subject to the broadband emission limits of 6.5, and production parts may deviate by at most 4 dB.

candidates.text: When a series-production rear lamp (ESA) is verified for conformity, its measured narrowband radiated emission levels shall not exceed the ESA narrowband reference limits of paragraph 6.6.2.1 by more than 4 dB (60 per cent). These limits are 52 to 42 dBµV/m (30–75 MHz), 42 to 53 dBµV/m (75–400 MHz) and 53 dBµV/m (400–1,000 MHz).
candidates.test_case: Measure narrowband radiated emissions of a production sample per Annex 8 and check that the levels are at or below the 6.6.2.1 limits + 4 dB.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's ESA is subject to the narrowband emission limits of 6.6, and production parts may deviate by at most 4 dB.

candidates.text: A series-production rear lamp (ESA) subjected to a radiated field strength of up to 80 per cent of the reference limits of paragraph 6.8.2.1 shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle that could be observed by the driver or other road users. This includes the stop lamp and rear position lamp functions.
candidates.test_case: Perform the Annex 9 radiated immunity test on a production sample at 80 % of the 6.8.2.1 field strength while monitoring the stop and rear position lamp outputs for any degradation.
candidates.applies_because: The stop and rear position lamp functions are immunity-related functions, so production parts must keep radiated immunity at 80 % of the type-approval level.

candidates.text: A series-production rear lamp (component or STU) shall show no degradation of performance of its immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) when subjected to conducted transient disturbances on the 12/24 V supply lines up to the levels given in paragraph 6.9.1.
candidates.test_case: Apply the Annex 10 conducted transient pulses at the 6.9.1 levels to a production sample and monitor the stop and rear position lamp functions for degradation.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's ESA connects to 12/24 V vehicle supply lines and carries immunity-related functions.

candidates.text: A series-production rear lamp (component or STU) shall not exceed the conducted transient emission levels given in paragraph 6.7.1 on its 12/24 V supply lines.
candidates.test_case: Measure conducted transient emissions of a production sample on the supply lines per Annex 10 and compare them with the 6.7.1 levels.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's LED drive electronics can generate conducted transients on the 12/24 V supply lines.

candidates.text: In case of an LED drive circuit not exempted under paragraph 6.10 (e.g. active switch-mode/PWM driver), the broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear lamp ESA, measured according to Annex 7 with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the Appendix 6 reference limits: E = 62 − 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m from 30 to 75 MHz; E = 52 + 15.13 log(F/75) dBµV/m from 75 to 400 MHz; E = 63 dBµV/m from 400 to 1,000 MHz.
candidates.test_case: Perform the Annex 7 ESA radiated broadband emission measurement (120 kHz bandwidth, 30–1,000 MHz) with the stop, rear position and reversing functions operating, and compare the results against the Appendix 6 limit line.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp's LED modules on PCB form an ESA whose broadband emission limits for ESA approval are defined in Appendix 6.

candidates.text: In case of an LED drive circuit containing narrowband sources (e.g. microcontroller, oscillator, clocked driver or data bus interface) not exempted under paragraph 6.10, the narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear lamp ESA, measured according to Annex 8 with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the Appendix 7 reference limits: E = 52 − 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m from 30 to 75 MHz; E = 42 + 15.13 log(F/75) dBµV/m from 75 to 400 MHz; E = 53 dBµV/m from 400 to 1,000 MHz.
candidates.test_case: Perform the Annex 8 ESA radiated narrowband emission measurement (120 kHz bandwidth, 30–1,000 MHz) with all lamp functions active, and compare the results against the Appendix 7 limit line.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp's ESA must meet the ESA narrowband emission limits, which are defined in Appendix 7, when its electronics generate narrowband emissions.

candidates.text: The broadband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp ESA (LED modules on PCB with driving circuitry) shall be measured according to CISPR 25, unless otherwise stated in Annex 7. This applies where the broadband emission test is not waived under the exceptions of paragraph 6.10, e.g. for a passive LED drive.
candidates.test_case: Perform the radiated broadband emission measurement on the lamp ESA per CISPR 25 and confirm that the test report references the Annex 7 method.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's LED electronics form an ESA whose broadband emissions are measured by the Annex 7 method referenced in paragraph 6.5.1.

candidates.text: During the broadband emission test the rear lamp ESA shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load, i.e. with the rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions energised.
candidates.test_case: Check the test set-up and report to confirm that all lamp functions are energised in normal operation at maximum load during the scan.
candidates.applies_because: This operating state defines the condition under which the lamp's emissions must stay below the limits.

candidates.text: For an ESA not involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', such as this rear lamp, the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25. As an alternative, an OATS complying with CISPR 16-1-4 may be used.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the emission test was carried out in an ALSE per CISPR 25 Clause 6.4, or in a compliant OATS.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is a 12/24 V ESA with no charging-mode function, so the ALSE method of CISPR 25 applies.

candidates.text: The rear lamp ESA shall meet the broadband emission limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz when measured in an ALSE or OATS. The limits are 62 to 52 dBµV/m from 30 to 75 MHz (decreasing logarithmically), 52 to 63 dBµV/m from 75 to 400 MHz (increasing logarithmically) and a constant 63 dBµV/m from 400 to 1,000 MHz.
candidates.test_case: Scan 30–1,000 MHz in horizontal and vertical polarisation and compare the readings with the paragraph 6.5.2.1 limit line.
candidates.applies_because: These are the pass criteria the lamp's emissions must satisfy for ESA type approval.

candidates.text: The broadband emission limits apply to quasi-peak detection. If peak detectors are used to measure the rear lamp ESA, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied before comparing the readings with the limits.
candidates.test_case: Check that peak readings were corrected by 20 dB, or that quasi-peak detection was used, before comparison with the limits.
candidates.applies_because: The detector basis determines whether the lamp's measured emissions pass the limits.

candidates.text: For the rear lamp ESA, the maximum of the readings relative to the limit, over horizontal and vertical polarisation, in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
candidates.test_case: Review the test data to confirm that the worst-case polarisation reading in each band is used as the characteristic value and lies below the limit.
candidates.applies_because: This defines which reading of the lamp is assessed against the limit.

candidates.text: The narrowband electromagnetic emission of the rear lamp ESA (LED modules on PCB with wiring/connector) shall be tested according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4 of CISPR 25. Any point not stated in Annex 8 follows CISPR 25. As an alternative, an OATS complying with CISPR 16-1-4 may be used.
candidates.test_case: Perform the narrowband radiated emission measurement in an ALSE per CISPR 25 clause 6.4 (or a CISPR 16-1-4 compliant OATS) and review the test report.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is an ESA other than one involved in REESS charging mode, and Annex 8 is the narrowband emission method referenced by para 6.6.

candidates.text: During the narrowband emission test, the rear lamp ESA shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load (e.g. rear position, stop and reversing functions energised at rated supply voltage).
candidates.test_case: Check the test set-up and log that all lamp functions are active at nominal 12 V/24 V supply, at maximum load, during the scan.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the operating state of the lamp electronics under which emission compliance must be shown.

candidates.text: The narrowband emission limits for the rear lamp ESA shall be met throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
candidates.test_case: Scan from 30 to 1,000 MHz and compare the emissions against the 6.6.2.1 limit line over the full range.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the frequency range over which the lamp's narrowband emissions must stay within the para 6.6.2.1 limits.

candidates.text: Narrowband emissions of the rear lamp ESA shall be assessed with an average detector.
candidates.test_case: Verify in the test report that the narrowband emission results were measured with an average detector.
candidates.applies_because: The detector type defines which emission value the lamp electronics must keep below the narrowband limit.

candidates.text: For the rear lamp ESA, the maximum of the readings relative to the limit, taken over horizontal and vertical antenna polarisation in each of the 14 frequency bands, shall be the characteristic reading at the measured frequency. This characteristic reading shall comply with the narrowband limit.
candidates.test_case: Measure in both horizontal and vertical polarisation and confirm that the worst-case reading in each band is below the limit.
candidates.applies_because: This defines which reading of the lamp's emission is compared with the limit, so emissions in both polarisations must comply.

candidates.text: For radiated immunity, the ESA (rear lamp) may comply with any combination of the following test methods, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that together they cover the full frequency range of 20 to 6,000 MHz: absorber chamber test (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell test (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection (ISO 11452-4), stripline test (ISO 11452-5) or reverberation chamber test (ISO 11452-11). Frequency range and general test conditions are based on ISO 11452-1.
candidates.test_case: Review the test plan and reports to confirm that the selected methods together cover 20–6,000 MHz without gaps.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp LED electronics are an ESA with immunity-related functions (stop and rear position lamps) and must pass ESA radiated immunity testing.

candidates.text: The ESA immunity test conditions shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
candidates.test_case: Check the test report for conformity of the test conditions (temperature, supply voltage, etc.) with ISO 11452-1.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the general test conditions under which the rear lamp ESA must demonstrate immunity.

candidates.text: During immunity testing, the ESA (rear lamp) shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition, i.e. with its stop lamp and rear position lamp functions active.
candidates.test_case: Verify during the test that the lamp is powered and its stop and rear position functions are activated and monitored.
candidates.applies_because: Immunity must be shown with the lamp's immunity-related functions operating.

candidates.text: The ESA shall be subjected to radiated immunity testing over the frequency range 20 to 6,000 MHz, with frequency step size and dwell time according to ISO 11452-1.
candidates.test_case: Perform the immunity sweep from 20 to 6,000 MHz with ISO 11452-1 steps and dwell times, and check the functions for deviations.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the frequency range of the RF stress the rear lamp ESA must withstand.

candidates.text: In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal shall be amplitude modulated (AM) with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, unless otherwise agreed between the Technical Service and the ESA manufacturer.
candidates.test_case: Expose the lamp to AM 1 kHz / 80 % signals from 20 to 400 MHz and monitor lamp operation.
candidates.applies_because: This is the modulation of the RF stress applied to the rear lamp ESA in this band.

candidates.text: In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal shall be pulse modulated PM2 with Ton 3 µs and a period of 3,333 µs, unless otherwise agreed between the Technical Service and the ESA manufacturer.
candidates.test_case: Expose the lamp to PM2 (3 µs on / 3,333 µs period) signals from 2,700 to 3,100 MHz and monitor lamp operation.
candidates.applies_because: This is the modulation of the RF stress applied to the rear lamp ESA in the radar band.

candidates.text: In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the immunity test signal shall be pulse modulated PM3 with Ton 500 µs and a period of 1,000 µs, unless otherwise agreed between the Technical Service and the ESA manufacturer.
candidates.test_case: Expose the lamp to PM3 (500 µs on / 1,000 µs period) signals in 380–2,700 MHz and 3,100–6,000 MHz and monitor lamp operation.
candidates.applies_because: This is the modulation of the RF stress applied to the rear lamp ESA in these bands.

candidates.text: In case the absorber chamber test is used, the ESA shall be exposed to antenna-generated radiation with the test field established by the substitution method according to ISO 11452-2 and with vertical polarization.
candidates.test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-2 absorber chamber test using vertical polarization and substitution-method field calibration.
candidates.applies_because: The absorber chamber is one of the permitted methods for showing the rear lamp's radiated immunity.

candidates.text: In case TEM cell testing is used, the ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-3, with maximum field coupling to either the ESA or its wiring harness.
candidates.test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-3 TEM cell test in the maximum-coupling orientation chosen by the Technical Service.
candidates.applies_because: TEM cell testing is a permitted method for the rear lamp ESA.

candidates.text: In case bulk current injection is used, the ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench, either by the substitution method with the injection probe 150 mm from the ESA or by the closed loop method with the injection probe 900 mm from the ESA.
candidates.test_case: Perform ISO 11452-4 BCI on the lamp harness with the probe at 150 mm (substitution) or 900 mm (closed loop).
candidates.applies_because: BCI is a permitted method for covering the low-frequency part of the rear lamp's immunity range.

candidates.text: As an alternative to bench BCI, the ESA may be tested while installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4, using the substitution method with the injection probe 150 mm from the ESA.
candidates.test_case: If chosen, perform in-vehicle BCI per ISO 11451-4 with the probe 150 mm from the lamp.
candidates.applies_because: This is a permitted alternative for demonstrating the rear lamp's BCI immunity.

candidates.text: In case stripline testing is used, the ESA wiring harness shall be subjected to the specified field strengths according to ISO 11452-5.
candidates.test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-5 stripline test on the lamp harness.
candidates.applies_because: Stripline testing is a permitted method for the rear lamp ESA.

candidates.text: In case the reverberation chamber test is used, the ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-11 using a test setup with ground plane, unless otherwise specified.
candidates.test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-11 reverberation chamber test with a ground-plane setup.
candidates.applies_because: The reverberation chamber is a permitted method for the rear lamp ESA.

candidates.text: The ESA shall be subjected to test pulse 1 according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines, as part of the immunity against transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines.
candidates.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 1 to the lamp supply and operationally connected inputs and check functional status against the immunity criteria of the regulation.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp's LED PCB is an ESA supplied from the 12/24 V vehicle supply.

candidates.text: The ESA shall be subjected to test pulse 2a according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
candidates.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 2a to the lamp supply and connected inputs and verify the lamp functions meet the required functional status.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp ESA is connected to the vehicle 12/24 V supply lines.

candidates.text: The ESA shall be subjected to test pulse 2b according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
candidates.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 2b to the lamp supply and connected inputs and verify the lamp functions meet the required functional status.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp ESA is connected to the vehicle 12/24 V supply lines.

candidates.text: The ESA shall be subjected to test pulse 3a according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
candidates.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 3a to the lamp supply and connected inputs and verify the stop and rear position lamp functions remain unaffected.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp ESA is connected to the vehicle 12/24 V supply lines.

candidates.text: The ESA shall be subjected to test pulse 3b according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
candidates.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 3b to the lamp supply and connected inputs and verify the stop and rear position lamp functions remain unaffected.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp ESA is connected to the vehicle 12/24 V supply lines.

candidates.text: The ESA shall be subjected to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2, applied to the supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
candidates.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the lamp supply and connected inputs and check the lamp's functional status during and after the profile.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp is intended for M1 vehicles that may have a 12 V/24 V starter motor.

candidates.text: In case the ESA is exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12 V/24 V starter motor), the ESA is not subject to the ISO 16750-2 starting profile test.
candidates.test_case: Check the manufacturer's declaration and the restrictions of use for exclusive EV fitment before omitting the starting profile test.
candidates.applies_because: This exemption applies to the rear lamp only if it is declared for exclusive use on electric vehicles without a starter motor.

candidates.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines, and on other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines, shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2.
candidates.test_case: Measure switching transient emissions of the lamp on its supply lines per ISO 7637-2 and compare them with the permitted values.
candidates.applies_because: The LED drive electronics of the rear lamp may generate conducted transients on the vehicle 12/24 V supply.

candidates.text: When the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp (and the retro-reflector) form one unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, each of these lamps shall satisfy the provisions of UN R148 or of another UN Regulation (e.g. R150 for the retro-reflector).
candidates.test_case: Check that each function in the unit holds a valid approval or passes the tests of its Regulation.
candidates.applies_because: The product is a rear combination unit grouping R148 lamp functions with an R150 retro-reflector.

candidates.text: A lamp that does not satisfy the provisions of any of those Regulations shall not be part of the unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
candidates.test_case: Review the unit's bill of functions against the approval reports and confirm there is no non-compliant lamp.
candidates.applies_because: Every lamp function in the combination must be approvable for the unit to be approved.

candidates.text: The lamp shall be identified by the approval symbols of its functions: R1 (rear position lamp, steady) or R2 (rear position lamp, variable intensity); S1 (stop lamp, steady) or S2 (stop lamp, variable intensity); AR (reversing lamp, letters A and R may be mingled).
candidates.test_case: Inspect the approval marking for the correct symbols matching each function variant.
candidates.applies_because: The product contains rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions that are identified by these symbols.

candidates.text: Every device of the approved type shall have a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings (trade name, light source category, rated voltage, module code, control gear identification).
candidates.test_case: Inspect the drawing and sample for a reserved marking area that accommodates all required markings.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is a device approved under R148 that must carry markings.

candidates.text: All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
candidates.test_case: Perform visual legibility inspection and a rub/durability check of the markings.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp carries approval and other markings.

candidates.text: The dimension "a" of the approval marking shall be at least 5 mm.
candidates.test_case: Measure the dimension "a" of the approval mark on the sample.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp carries an R148 approval mark.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which granted approval.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled E and country number.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp carries the R148 approval marking.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number forming part of the approval number.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for a four to six-digit sequential number matching the approval.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp carries the R148 approval marking.

candidates.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the position of the sequential number relative to the circled E.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp carries the R148 approval marking.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light-signalling lamp functions (R1/R2, S1/S2, AR).
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the function symbols.
candidates.applies_because: The product's lamp functions must be identified on the marking.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits of the series of amendments in force at the time of approval (e.g. 148R01).
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for "148R" followed by the series digits.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp carries the R148 approval marking.

candidates.text: In case the lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the approval marking shall include a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
candidates.test_case: For a side-specific design, inspect the marking for the horizontal arrow.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamp may be side-specific (open option on mounting side marking).

candidates.text: In case of a side-specific lamp, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle for the rear position lamp.
candidates.test_case: Check on the mounted lamp that the arrow points outboard.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a rear position lamp.

candidates.text: In case the reversing lamp has a reduced light distribution for fitment of two reversing lamps, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: For a reduced-distribution reversing lamp, check that the arrow points outboard.
candidates.applies_because: The reversing lamp may have a reduced light distribution for two-lamp fitment (open option).

candidates.text: In case the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right of the function symbol.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for "D" to the right of the relevant symbol.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp may be designed as an assembly of two independent lamps (open option D).

candidates.text: In case the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamp system, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right of the function symbol.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for "Y" to the right of the relevant symbol.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp may be part of an interdependent lamp system (open option Y).

candidates.text: In case a lamp function has a reduced light distribution (Annex 3, paragraph 1.1, e.g. mounting height ≤ 750 mm), the marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
candidates.test_case: For a reduced-distribution approval, inspect the marking for the downward arrow from a horizontal segment.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position or stop lamp functions may be approved with reduced light distribution.

candidates.text: The lamp shall bear the approval marking.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the sample for presence of the approval marking.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is type-approved under R148.

candidates.text: The lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the sample for the trade name or mark.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is type-approved under R148.

candidates.text: In case of non-replaceable LED light sources, the lamp is exempt from bearing a marking of the category of light source(s).
candidates.test_case: Confirm the light source type; no light source category marking is required.
candidates.applies_because: The product uses non-replaceable LED light sources.

candidates.text: The lamp shall bear a marking of the rated voltage(s) (6 V, 12 V or 24 V) or the range of voltage, since it has non-replaceable light sources (and/or an electronic light source control gear, variable luminous intensity control or secondary operating mode).
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage or voltage range marking.
candidates.applies_because: The product has non-replaceable LED light sources and possibly variable intensity control.

candidates.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the module for the trade name or mark.
candidates.applies_because: The light source may be a replaceable module (open option).

candidates.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear its specific identification code: "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle, followed by additional symbols or characters if several non-identical modules are used. The approval mark may differ from that on the lamp but shall be from the same applicant.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the module code format and compare it with the lamp approval.
candidates.applies_because: The light source may be a replaceable module (open option).

candidates.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear its rated voltage(s) or range of voltage.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the module for the voltage marking.
candidates.applies_because: The light source may be a replaceable module (open option).

candidates.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the module MD code.
candidates.applies_because: The light source may be a replaceable module (open option).

candidates.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or range of voltage.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the voltage marking.
candidates.applies_because: The light source may be a replaceable module (open option).

candidates.text: In case an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body, it shall be marked with its identification number and the name of its manufacturer.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the external control unit for the identification number and manufacturer name.
candidates.applies_because: The control gear / variable intensity control may be external but declared part of the lamp (open option).

candidates.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent light-emitting part of the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking location and confirm the marked part is not separable from the outer lens.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp carries the approval marking.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the boot lid or a door is opened.
candidates.test_case: Check visibility of the marking on the vehicle installation or a mock-up.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is installed at the rear exterior of an M1 vehicle.

candidates.text: In case the outer lens is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
candidates.test_case: If the lens is detachable, inspect both the lens and the housing for the approval marking.
candidates.applies_because: The outer lens is a separate PMMA component that could be designed as detachable.

candidates.text: In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bears different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
candidates.test_case: Inspect each main body for markings limited to its own functions.
candidates.applies_because: The outer lens may be shared across several device types.

candidates.text: The approval marking, the trade name, the light source category (if any), the rated voltage, the module identification code and voltage on the lamp (if any) and the external control gear marking (if any) shall be affixed on the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp for all the applicable markings.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp carries these markings.

candidates.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, the module markings (trade name, MD identification code, rated voltage) shall be affixed on the module itself.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the module for its markings.
candidates.applies_because: The light source may be a replaceable module (open option).

candidates.text: The trade name, the light source category, the rated voltage, the module markings and the control gear markings do not need to be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle.
candidates.applies_because: This relaxation applies to the lamp's non-approval markings.

candidates.text: Where the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (including the R150 retro-reflector) comply with several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed anywhere on the unit, subject to the conditions of paragraphs 3.3.5.1.1 and 3.3.5.1.2.
candidates.test_case: If a single mark is used, inspect its content and position.
candidates.applies_because: The product groups R148 lamp functions with an R150 retro-reflector.

candidates.text: Where a single approval mark is used for the grouped/combined/reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after installation.
candidates.test_case: Check the visibility of the single mark on the installed lamp.
candidates.applies_because: This proviso applies to the single combined mark option.

candidates.text: Where a single approval mark is used, no light-transmitting part of the grouped/combined/reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the construction to confirm the light-transmitting parts cannot be removed without removing the mark.
candidates.applies_because: This proviso applies to the single combined mark option.

candidates.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations (R148, R150) under which approval has been granted.
candidates.test_case: Measure the mark components and compare them with the minimum sizes of R148 and R150.
candidates.applies_because: The product may carry a single combined R148/R150 approval mark.

candidates.text: Each lamp function (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5 of UN R148.
candidates.test_case: Review the type-approval test report covering all paragraph 4 and 5 checks for each function.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamp is submitted for R148 approval for its R, S and AR functions.

candidates.text: The general and individual specifications (sections 5 and 6 and referenced annexes) of UN R48 in force at the time of application shall apply to each lamp function for vehicle category M1, where their verification at lamp type approval is feasible.
candidates.test_case: Check the lamp against applicable R48 §5/§6 requirements, e.g. geometric visibility and colour, during approval testing.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is intended for M1 vehicles, whose installation is governed by R48.

candidates.text: The lamp shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which it may be subjected, its satisfactory operation remains assured and it retains the characteristics prescribed by R148.
candidates.test_case: Vibration test of the mounted lamp followed by functional and photometric re-check.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is mounted on the vehicle exterior and exposed to vibration in service.

candidates.text: A lamp approved as a rear position lamp is deemed also to be approved as a rear end-outline marker lamp.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a rear position lamp function.

candidates.text: The rear position lamp, being grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp and reversing lamp, may also be used as an end-outline marker lamp.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position lamp is grouped or reciprocally incorporated with other functions in one housing.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with another function using a common light source and is designed to operate permanently with an additional intensity-regulating system, this arrangement is permitted.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the circuit design and verify the intensity regulation in both function modes.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is a reciprocally incorporated rear position/stop lamp with shared LEDs.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, these functions shall either be provided by multiple light sources or be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure of the lamps.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the LED circuit for separate light sources per function, or verify the declared tell-tale failure-signal output.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is reciprocal incorporation of the R and S functions.

candidates.text: In case a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the internal optical structure or outer lens texture within the apparent surface of the rear position lamp, only one logo may be incorporated, all requirements for the rear position lamp function shall still be fulfilled, and the logo shall be only that of the brand name of the vehicle or body manufacturer.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the logo and the manufacturer statement, and repeat full photometry of the rear position lamp with the logo present.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is a vehicle manufacturer logo in the rear position lamp.

candidates.text: In case a logo is incorporated, the enclosed light-emitting surface of the logo (transparent and non-transparent components) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
candidates.test_case: Measure the projected logo light-emitting area in the reference axis direction.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is a logo in the rear position lamp, limited to a maximum of 100 cm2.

candidates.text: Notwithstanding paragraph 5.5.2 of UN R48, the logo light-emitting surface does not have to be symmetrical by itself.
candidates.applies_because: This relaxation applies if the logo option is chosen.

candidates.text: The stop lamp and the reversing lamp functions shall not incorporate a logo.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the apparent surfaces of the stop and reversing lamp functions for the absence of any logo.
candidates.applies_because: The product contains stop and reversing lamp functions.

candidates.text: In a lamp function containing more than one LED light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.
candidates.test_case: Analyse the LED circuit topology (series strings) to identify the light-source groups for the failure analysis.
candidates.applies_because: Each function uses multiple LEDs on the PCB.

candidates.text: In case of failure of any one light source in a lamp function containing more than one light source (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp), either the light intensity shall still comply with the minimum intensities of the pertinent Annex 3 standard light distribution while the maximum intensities are not exceeded with all light sources lit, or a signal for activation of a failure tell-tale per R48 (e.g. 6.4.8, 6.7.8, 6.10.8) shall be produced.
candidates.test_case: Disable each LED group in turn and measure photometry against minimum values, or verify the tell-tale failure-signal output.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp functions use multiple LED light sources, and the failure-detection open option covers both alternatives.

candidates.text: In case of a rear position lamp of category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, failure of the variable intensity control shall automatically result in fulfilment of the steady luminous intensity requirements of category R1.
candidates.test_case: Simulate a failure of the variable intensity control and measure that the intensities fall within the R1 limits.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is a variable-intensity R2 rear position lamp.

candidates.text: In case of a stop lamp of category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, failure of the variable intensity control shall automatically result in fulfilment of the steady luminous intensity requirements of category S1.
candidates.test_case: Simulate a failure of the variable intensity control and measure that the intensities fall within the S1 limits.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is a variable-intensity S2 stop lamp.

candidates.text: The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light sources approved to UN R37, R99 and/or R128 (without use restriction), and/or light source modules, and/or non-replaceable light sources.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the light source design and documentation.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp uses LED light sources (non-replaceable LEDs or a light source module).

candidates.text: The lamp (light-signalling device) shall not generate radiated or power-line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: EMC emission tests (radiated and conducted) per R10 ESA methods.
candidates.applies_because: The LED modules and driving circuitry are an electronic sub-assembly.

candidates.text: In case of a replaceable light source module, the module shall only be fittable in the designated and correct position and shall only be removable with the use of tool(s).
candidates.test_case: Attempt incorrect fitment and tool-free removal of the module.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is a replaceable light source module.

candidates.text: In case of a replaceable light source module, the module shall be tamperproof.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the module design for tamper resistance.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is a replaceable light source module.

candidates.text: In case of a replaceable light source module, regardless of the use of tools, the module shall not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN-approved light source or with any other replaceable light source module of different characteristics in the same lamp housing.
candidates.test_case: Attempt cross-fitting of other modules and UN-approved light sources into each module position.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is a replaceable light source module.

candidates.text: In case of a replaceable light source module, when the module is replaced by another module from the applicant bearing the same identification code, the photometric requirements of the lamp shall be met.
candidates.test_case: Swap in a second module with the same MD code and repeat the photometric measurements.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is a replaceable light source module.

candidates.text: Photometric and colorimetric compliance shall be achieved with the non-replaceable light sources or light source modules present in the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Photometric and colorimetric measurement of the complete lamp with its own LEDs.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp uses non-replaceable LEDs or LED modules.

candidates.text: Where the lamp may be installed in more than one position or a field of positions, the photometric requirements shall be met in each position or at the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
candidates.test_case: Repeat photometry for each declared mounting position or the extreme positions.
candidates.applies_because: This binds the lamp if the manufacturer specifies several mounting positions.

candidates.text: Unless otherwise specified, the luminous intensities shall be met with the light sources continuously lit.
candidates.test_case: Measure intensities with the LEDs continuously powered.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the operating state for the photometry of all the lamp functions.

candidates.text: The intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation is deemed satisfied if it is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from that direction.
candidates.test_case: In case of challenge, check the intensity within ±0.25° of the test point.
candidates.applies_because: This is a pass-criterion tolerance for the lamp's photometry.

candidates.text: For a 12 V system, the lamp functions shall meet the photometric requirements with 13.5 V supplied at the lamp, unless otherwise specified.
candidates.test_case: Supply 13.5 V at the lamp connector during photometric testing.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is intended for M1 vehicles, normally with a 12 V system.

candidates.text: In case the lamp is intended for a 24 V system, the lamp functions shall meet the photometric requirements with 28 V supplied at the lamp, unless otherwise specified.
candidates.test_case: Supply 28 V at the lamp connector during photometric testing.
candidates.applies_because: This applies if the lamp is declared for 24 V systems.

candidates.text: In case the lamp is controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall meet the requirements when operated as specified by the applicant.
candidates.test_case: Operate the lamp with the declared control gear and settings during testing.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is an electronic control gear or variable intensity control.

candidates.text: In case the lamp with non-replaceable light sources or light source modules is not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, the lamp shall meet the requirements when operated as specified by the applicant.
candidates.test_case: Operate the lamp at the applicant-declared supply conditions during testing.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is LEDs without separate control gear.

candidates.text: The luminous intensity of each lamp function, on each of the two samples, shall on the reference axis (HV) be not less than the minimum specified in the pertinent table of paragraph 5 (Table 4 for R1/R2, stop lamp table for S1/S2, reversing lamp table for AR).
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement at HV for each function on both samples.
candidates.applies_because: The product has rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions.

candidates.text: The luminous intensity of each lamp function shall in no direction where the lamp is visible exceed the maximum specified in the pertinent table of paragraph 5.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric scan of the full visible field for each function, compared with the maximum values.
candidates.applies_because: Maximum intensity limits apply to all R148 functions of the lamp.

candidates.text: Outside the reference axis, the luminous intensity of each lamp function shall be not less than the minimum of the pertinent paragraph 5 table multiplied by the percentage given in the pertinent Annex 3 light distribution figure (Figure A3-I for R and S), or not less than the absolute value given in that figure (Figure A3-V for AR).
candidates.test_case: Measure the Annex 3 grid points for each function and compare with the derived minima.
candidates.applies_because: Standard light distributions apply to each lamp function.

candidates.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Annex 2, the luminous intensity of each lamp function shall be not less than the minimum specified for geometric visibility in the pertinent table of paragraph 5.
candidates.test_case: Measure intensity across the Annex 2 geometric visibility field for each function.
candidates.applies_because: Geometric visibility minima apply to the lamp functions.

candidates.text: The provisions of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed for each lamp function.
candidates.test_case: Check intermediate grid directions against the lowest surrounding minimum (50 % rule for AR).
candidates.applies_because: Local uniformity provisions apply to the R, S and AR distributions.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp or stop lamp is approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D" deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the maximum intensity requirement when all lamps together are lit.
candidates.test_case: Measure maximum intensities with both lamps of the assembly lit.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is an assembly of two independent lamps (D).

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp or stop lamp is approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D", it shall comply with the minimum intensity requirement if either lamp has failed.
candidates.test_case: Measure minimum intensities with each lamp of the assembly switched off in turn.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is an assembly of two independent lamps (D).

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp or stop lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system marked "Y", the system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
candidates.test_case: Photometric and colorimetric test with all interdependent lamps operated together.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is an interdependent lamp system (Y).

candidates.text: In case the interdependent rear position lamp system is partly mounted on a fixed and partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component, the inboard visibility being deemed satisfied if they still meet the photometric values of the light distribution field at those positions.
candidates.test_case: Photometric and visibility measurement at each fixed position of the movable component.
candidates.applies_because: This applies if the Y option is used on a tailgate/boot-lid split lamp.

candidates.text: In case of a variable-intensity rear position lamp (R2) or stop lamp (S2), the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
candidates.test_case: Measure intensities over the full control range and compare with the paragraph 5 limits.
candidates.applies_because: Open options include R2/S2 variable-intensity functions.

candidates.text: In case of a variable intensity control depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, it shall not cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady (R1/S1) maximum under night-time conditions.
candidates.test_case: Set the control to night-time mode and measure the maximum intensity against the R1/S1 maximum.
candidates.applies_because: Open options include R2/S2 variable-intensity control.

candidates.text: In case of other variable intensity control systems, the control shall not cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady (R1/S1) maximum under standard conditions (MOR > 2,000 m, clean lens).
candidates.test_case: Set the control to standard-condition inputs and measure the maximum intensity.
candidates.applies_because: Open options include R2/S2 variable-intensity control.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the ratio between the intensities measured with both turned on simultaneously and with the rear position lamp alone should be at least 5:1 within ±5° V and ±10° H, with all light sources in operation where a function has several light sources considered as a single lamp.
candidates.test_case: Measure intensities with R alone and with R+S over the ±10° H / ±5° V field and compute the ratio at each point.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is reciprocal incorporation of the R and S functions.

candidates.text: Luminous intensity compliance of each lamp function shall be demonstrated in tests carried out according to Annex 8.
candidates.test_case: Perform the Annex 8 test sequence (e.g. stabilisation, operating conditions) before photometry.
candidates.applies_because: This binds the photometric verification of all lamp functions.

candidates.text: The colour of the light emitted by each function (red for rear position and stop lamps, white for reversing lamp) shall meet the requirements when measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for that function in Annex 3, using the test procedure of paragraph 4.8.
candidates.test_case: Spectroradiometric chromaticity measurement at grid points for each function.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp emits red and white light through its PMMA lens and LEDs.

candidates.text: Outside the field of the light distribution grid, no sharp variation of the colour of light emitted by each function shall be observed.
candidates.test_case: Visual and colorimetric check of colour uniformity outside the grid field.
candidates.applies_because: This applies to all signal functions of the lamp.

candidates.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements of Table 4.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples at HV, across the Figure A3-I grid and within the geometric visibility angles, compared against Table 4.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a rear position lamp of category R1 or R2.

candidates.text: In case of a steady rear position lamp (R1): the minimum luminous intensity on the reference axis shall be 4 cd. The maximum luminous intensity in any direction where the lamp is visible shall be 17 cd for a single lamp, or 8.5 cd for a lamp marked "D". The standard light distribution shall follow Figure A3-I. The minimum intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 shall be 0.05 cd.
candidates.test_case: Photometric measurement of R1 samples at 13.5 V (or as specified) against the Table 4 R1 values.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the rear position lamp may be steady category R1.

candidates.text: In case of a variable intensity rear position lamp (R2): the minimum luminous intensity on the reference axis shall be 4 cd. The maximum luminous intensity in any direction where the lamp is visible shall be 42 cd for a single lamp, or 21 cd for a lamp marked "D". The standard light distribution shall follow Figure A3-I. The minimum intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 shall be 0.05 cd.
candidates.test_case: Photometric measurement of R2 samples over the full variable intensity range against the Table 4 R2 values.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the rear position lamp may be variable intensity category R2.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, a luminous intensity of 60 cd is permitted for the rear position lamp below a plane forming an angle of 5° downward from the horizontal plane.
candidates.test_case: Measure rear position lamp intensity below 5°D and check that it is at most 60 cd where this relaxation is used.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the rear position and stop lamps may be reciprocally incorporated.

candidates.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall emit at least 0.05 cd within its angles of geometric visibility. These angles are 45° inboard and 80° outboard horizontally, reduced to 20° inboard below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm. Vertically they are 15° above and 15° below, reduced to 5° below for a mounting height of the H-plane below 750 mm.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometer scan over the Table A2-1 angular field for R1/R2, checking for at least 0.05 cd at every direction.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position lamp is subject to the geometric visibility minimum of Table 4.

candidates.text: The rear position lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
candidates.test_case: Simulate failure of a single LED or LED string and verify compliance with paragraph 4.6 (minimum intensity maintained or tell-tale signal produced).
candidates.applies_because: The rear position lamp contains multiple LED light sources.

candidates.text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
candidates.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the emitted light, checking the chromaticity coordinates against the red limits.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a rear position lamp.

candidates.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the stop lamp shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements of Table 7.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples at HV, across the Figure A3-I grid and within the geometric visibility angles, compared against Table 7.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a stop lamp of category S1 or S2.

candidates.text: In case of a steady stop lamp (S1): the minimum luminous intensity on the reference axis shall be 60 cd. The maximum luminous intensity shall be 260 cd for a single lamp, or 130 cd for a lamp marked "D". The standard light distribution shall follow Figure A3-I. The minimum intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 shall be 0.3 cd.
candidates.test_case: Photometric measurement of S1 samples against the Table 7 S1 values.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the stop lamp may be steady category S1.

candidates.text: In case of a variable intensity stop lamp (S2): the minimum luminous intensity on the reference axis shall be 60 cd. The maximum luminous intensity shall be 730 cd for a single lamp, or 365 cd for a lamp marked "D". The standard light distribution shall follow Figure A3-I. The minimum intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 shall be 0.3 cd (day) and 0.07 cd (night).
candidates.test_case: Photometric measurement of S2 samples in day and night modes against the Table 7 S2 values.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the stop lamp may be variable intensity category S2.

candidates.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall meet the Table 7 minimum intensity within its angles of geometric visibility. These angles are 45° inboard and 45° outboard horizontally, reduced to 20° inboard below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.
