Vertically they are 15° above and 15° below, reduced to 5° below for a mounting height of the H-plane below 750 mm.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometer scan over the Table A2-1 stop lamp angular field, checking the 0.3 cd (S2 night: 0.07 cd) minimum.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp is subject to the geometric visibility minimum of Table 7.

candidates.text: The stop lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
candidates.test_case: Simulate failure of a single LED or LED string and verify compliance with paragraph 4.6.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp contains multiple LED light sources.

candidates.text: The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
candidates.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the stop lamp light against the red chromaticity limits.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a stop lamp.

candidates.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements of Table 10.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples over the Figure A3-V grid, compared against Table 10.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a reversing lamp of category AR.

candidates.text: The reversing lamp (AR) shall have a minimum luminous intensity on the reference axis of 80 cd. It shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V outside the reference axis.
candidates.test_case: Measure intensity at HV and at the Figure A3-V points, checking each against its minimum.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a reversing lamp of category AR.

candidates.text: The luminous intensity of the reversing lamp (AR) shall not exceed 300 cd in or above the H-plane. It shall not exceed 600 cd below the H-plane down to 5°D. It shall not exceed 8,000 cd below 5°D.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometer scan of all visible directions, checking the maximum in each vertical zone.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a reversing lamp of category AR.

candidates.text: In case the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices (reduced light distribution), the photometric intensity may be verified only up to 30° inwards, where at least 25 cd shall be satisfied. This condition shall be clearly explained in the application documents.
candidates.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp distribution up to 30° inboard and verify at least 25 cd there.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the reversing lamp may use the reduced light distribution for two-lamp fitment.

candidates.text: The reversing lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
candidates.test_case: Simulate failure of a single LED or LED string and verify compliance with paragraph 4.6.
candidates.applies_because: The reversing lamp contains multiple LED light sources.

candidates.text: The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
candidates.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the reversing lamp light against the white chromaticity limits.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a reversing lamp behind a clear window.

candidates.text: Rear position, stop and reversing lamps shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under UN R148, including the photometric and colorimetric requirements of paragraph 5.
candidates.test_case: Take random production lamps and compare their construction, photometry and colour with the approved type documentation and paragraph 5 requirements.
candidates.applies_because: Every series-produced lamp of the approved R148 type must conform to that type.

candidates.text: In conformity of production testing, no measured photometric value of a production rear position lamp (R1/R2), stop lamp (S1/S2) or reversing lamp (AR) shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in UN R148.
candidates.test_case: Measure luminous intensities of production lamps at the Annex 3 points per paragraph 4.8 and check that each value is within 20 % of the prescribed minimum and maximum values.
candidates.applies_because: This is the permitted performance deviation for production lamps of each R148 function in this rear combination lamp.

candidates.text: For the minimum luminous intensities required throughout the fields of geometric visibility (Annex 2) and the light distribution (Annex 3), the measured values of production lamps shall be at least the 20 per cent equivalents of Table 12: 7∙10^-1 cd → 5∙10^-1 cd; 6∙10^-1 cd → 4∙10^-1 cd; 3∙10^-1 cd → 2∙10^-1 cd; 7∙10^-2 cd → 5∙10^-2 cd; 5∙10^-2 cd → 3∙10^-2 cd. For example, the rear position lamp's 5∙10^-2 cd within the angles of geometric visibility becomes 3∙10^-2 cd.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of production samples at the geometric-visibility boundary directions, comparing each value with the Table 12 20 % equivalent value.
candidates.applies_because: The R1/R2, S1/S2 and AR functions have small minimum intensities within the geometric-visibility fields, and Table 12 sets their production equivalents.

candidates.text: The light emitted by production lamps shall comply with the required chromaticity coordinates (red for the rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp) when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of production samples per paragraph 4.9 with a spectroradiometer and check them against the red and white colour boundaries.
candidates.applies_because: Conformity of production covers the colorimetric characteristics of each lamp function.

candidates.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 80° outboard. These angles are shown for a lamp mounted on the right side of the vehicle and are mirrored for the left side.
candidates.test_case: Check by goniometric measurement or apparent-surface visibility analysis that the light-emitting surface is visible over 45° inboard to 80° outboard horizontally.
candidates.applies_because: The product contains a rear position lamp of class R1 or R2 listed in Table A2-1.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp (R1, R2) is to be mounted with its H-plane below 750 mm, the minimum horizontal inboard angle below the H-plane may be reduced to 20°, with the outboard angle remaining 80°.
candidates.test_case: Verify visibility below the H-plane over 20° inboard to 80° outboard for the declared low mounting height.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamp of an M1 car may be mounted with its H-plane below 750 mm.

candidates.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.
candidates.test_case: Check by goniometric measurement that the light-emitting surface is visible from 15° above to 15° below the H-plane.
candidates.applies_because: The product contains a rear position lamp of class R1 or R2 listed in Table A2-1.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp (R1, R2) is to be installed with its H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility may be reduced to 15° above and 5° below.
candidates.test_case: Verify visibility from 15° above to 5° below the H-plane for the declared low mounting height.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamp of an M1 car may be mounted below 750 mm.

candidates.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 45° outboard. These angles are shown for a lamp mounted on the right side of the vehicle and are mirrored for the left side.
candidates.test_case: Check by goniometric measurement that the stop lamp light-emitting surface is visible over 45° inboard to 45° outboard horizontally.
candidates.applies_because: The product contains a stop lamp of class S1 or S2 listed in Table A2-1.

candidates.text: In case the stop lamp (S1, S2) is to be mounted with its H-plane below 750 mm, the minimum horizontal inboard angle below the H-plane may be reduced to 20°, with the outboard angle remaining 45°.
candidates.test_case: Verify stop lamp visibility below the H-plane over 20° inboard to 45° outboard for the declared low mounting height.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamp of an M1 car may be mounted with its H-plane below 750 mm.

candidates.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.
candidates.test_case: Check by goniometric measurement that the stop lamp is visible from 15° above to 15° below the H-plane.
candidates.applies_because: The product contains a stop lamp of class S1 or S2 listed in Table A2-1.

candidates.text: In case the stop lamp (S1, S2) is to be installed with its H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility may be reduced to 15° above and 5° below.
candidates.test_case: Verify stop lamp visibility from 15° above to 5° below the H-plane for the declared low mounting height.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamp of an M1 car may be mounted below 750 mm.

candidates.text: For the rear position lamp and the stop lamp, the luminous intensity in each direction of measurement shall be at least the percentage given in the applicable standard light distribution figure of the minimum intensity required for that function, with the resulting values mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at each grid direction, compared with the percentage of the required minimum intensity rounded down to three significant digits.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position and stop lamp functions are verified against percentage-based standard light distributions in Annex 3.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) of 750 mm or less above the ground, its photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
candidates.test_case: Check the declared mounting height and limit the downward photometric verification to 5° below H when the height is 750 mm or less.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a rear position lamp that may be mounted at 750 mm or less on an M1 car.

candidates.text: In case the stop lamp (category S1 or S2) is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) of 750 mm or less above the ground, its photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
candidates.test_case: Check the declared mounting height and limit the downward photometric verification to 5° below H when the height is 750 mm or less.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes an S1/S2 stop lamp that may be mounted at 750 mm or less.

candidates.text: Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp and the stop lamp in each direction inside a part of the field bounded by grid lines shall be at least the lowest minimum percentage value shown on the grid lines surrounding that direction.
candidates.test_case: Scan intermediate directions between grid points goniophotometrically and confirm each intensity is at least the lowest surrounding grid minimum.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position and stop lamps are assessed against the grid-based standard light distribution.

candidates.text: If visual examination of the reversing lamp reveals substantial local variations of intensity, no luminous intensity measured between two of the prescribed directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower of the two minimum intensities prescribed for those directions.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the reversing lamp beam, and where local variations appear, measure intensities between adjacent measuring points and compare them with 50 % of the lower prescribed minimum.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a reversing lamp (AR).

candidates.text: The rear position lamp (R1/R2) shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, i.e. in each direction of measurement at least the percentage given in Figure A3-I of the minimum intensity required in Table 4.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at all Figure A3-I points, compared with the percentage of the Table 4 minimum.
candidates.applies_because: Figure A3-I is the standard light distribution prescribed for rear position lamps.

candidates.text: The stop lamp (S1 or S2) shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, i.e. in each direction of measurement at least the percentage given in Figure A3-I of the minimum intensity required in Table 7 (60 cd).
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at all Figure A3-I points, compared with the percentage of 60 cd.
candidates.applies_because: Figure A3-I is the standard light distribution prescribed for S1 and S2 stop lamps.

candidates.text: The reversing lamp shall emit, in each measuring point of Figure A3-V (angles relative to the reference axis passing through the centre of reference), at least the minimum luminous intensity in cd given in Figure A3-V.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of the reversing lamp at each Figure A3-V point, compared with the minimum cd values.
candidates.applies_because: Figure A3-V is the standard light distribution for reversing lamps, which the product includes.

candidates.text: Mass-produced rear combination lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) shall differ from the approved type, from a mechanical and geometric standpoint, by no more than inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Dimensional inspection of random production lamps against the approved type drawings.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is series-produced under an R148 approval and must conform to the approved type.

candidates.text: Any production lamp chosen at random shall meet the photometric performance requirements for each of its functions (rear position, stop, reversing) when tested according to paragraph 4.8, with the non-replaceable LED light sources or light source modules present in the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of random production lamps at the Annex 3 points for each function and comparison with paragraph 5 and CoP limits.
candidates.applies_because: Photometric conformity of production applies to every R148 function of this lamp.

candidates.text: Production lamps shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates (red for rear position and stop lamp, white for reversing lamp) when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
candidates.test_case: Spectroradiometric colour measurement of random production lamps within the light distribution field of each function.
candidates.applies_because: The colour of light emitted by each function must be maintained in series production.

candidates.text: Mass-produced rear combination lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) shall conform mechanically and geometrically to the approved type, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations.
candidates.test_case: Measure dimensions and inspect the construction of random production lamps against the approved drawings.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is series-produced under an R148 approval and must match the approved type mechanically and geometrically.

candidates.text: For each function (rear position, stop and reversing lamp), when any production lamp chosen at random is tested for photometric performance according to paragraph 4.8, no measured luminous intensity value shall deviate unfavourably by more than the values permitted in paragraph 6.1.3, i.e. 20 per cent from the prescribed values, or the Table 12 equivalents for the minimum values in the fields of Annexes 2 and 3.
candidates.test_case: Measure the luminous intensity of each function of a random production lamp at 13.5 V or the applicant-specified operation, with the non-replaceable LEDs present, and check that no value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent.
candidates.applies_because: Each LED lamp function of the product is subject to photometric conformity of production under R148.

candidates.text: Production lamps shall comply with the prescribed chromaticity coordinates (red for the rear position and stop lamp, white for the reversing lamp) when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of each function within its light distribution field, with the LEDs present in the lamp, and compare them with the colour boundaries.
candidates.applies_because: The red and white light emitted by the production lamp functions must stay within the R148 colour limits.

candidates.text: For the reversing lamp (LED technology), the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
candidates.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp intensity distribution after 1 min and 10 min of operation and compare it with the minimum and maximum values.
candidates.applies_because: The reversing lamp function uses LED light sources, not incandescent technology.

candidates.text: For the rear position lamp (R1/R2) using LED technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
candidates.test_case: Measure the rear position lamp intensities after 1 min and after 30 min (or at photometric stability) and check the minimum and maximum limits.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position lamp is an LED lamp other than a reversing or manoeuvring lamp.

candidates.text: For the stop lamp (S1/S2) using LED technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
candidates.test_case: Measure the stop lamp intensities after 1 min and after 30 min (or at photometric stability) and check the minimum and maximum limits.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp is an LED lamp other than a reversing or manoeuvring lamp.

candidates.text: In addition to the checks of paragraph 1, the luminous intensity distribution of each lamp function shall comply at the point in time after switch ON listed in Table A8-1 for that function, depending on the light source technology.
candidates.test_case: Check the intensity distribution at the Table A8-1 time after switch ON, or confirm the deemed-compliance condition for LED-only functions.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp includes rear position, stop and reversing functions, all of which are listed in Table A8-1.

candidates.text: Rear position lamp (also deemed end-outline marker lamp): the intensity requirements shall be met 4 s after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
candidates.test_case: Measure the intensity at HV 4 s after switch ON and scale the distribution to verify compliance.
candidates.applies_because: The product incorporates a rear position lamp, which is also deemed an end-outline marker lamp.

candidates.text: Stop lamp: the intensity requirements shall be met 0.2 s after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
candidates.test_case: Measure the intensity at HV 0.2 s after switch ON with a fast photometer and verify compliance.
candidates.applies_because: The product incorporates a stop lamp.

candidates.text: Reversing lamp: the intensity requirements shall be met 0.2 s after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
candidates.test_case: Measure the intensity at HV 0.2 s after switch ON and verify compliance.
candidates.applies_because: The product incorporates a reversing lamp.

candidates.text: Where a lamp function uses LED technology only, the lamp function is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2 are compliant.
candidates.test_case: Confirm that each function uses LED technology only and that the paragraph 1.2 measurements comply.
candidates.applies_because: All functions use only non-replaceable LED light sources or LED modules.

candidates.text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the minimum intensity requirements of each lamp function shall be met at all points in time, from the point in time listed in Table A8-1 until photometric stability is reached.
candidates.test_case: Record the intensity at the reference coordinate continuously from the Table A8-1 time until photometric stability and verify the minimum is never undercut.
candidates.applies_because: The LED driver circuitry may show unexpected run-up behaviour that triggers this check.

candidates.text: In case the lamp housing containing the retro-reflector is watertight, the retro-reflector shall be identified by the symbol "IA" (retro-reflector for motor vehicles, independent).
candidates.test_case: Inspect the approval marking on the lamp and the approval documents for the symbol "IA".
candidates.applies_because: The rear retro-reflector is approved as Class IA when the lamp it sits in is watertight.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector is combined with signal lamps which are not watertight, the retro-reflector shall be identified by the symbol "IB".
candidates.test_case: Inspect the approval marking on the lamp and the approval documents for the symbol "IB".
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is integrated in a combined rear lamp, so it is Class IB if the housing is not watertight.

candidates.text: Every retro-reflector of an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2., or for the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
candidates.test_case: Check the lens/housing drawing and a sample for a marking area large enough for the full marking at the minimum size.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector of the rear lamp must carry an R150 approval marking or a Unique Identifier.

candidates.text: All markings on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible and indelible.
candidates.test_case: Visually check legibility and perform a rub/indelibility check on the markings.
candidates.applies_because: This applies to all R150 markings on the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The size of the approval marking of a Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall be based on a minimum dimension "a" of 5 mm.
candidates.test_case: Measure the dimension "a" of the approval mark on the sample.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is Class IA or IB, and Table 1 sets a minimum "a" of 5 mm for these classes.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled E and the country number.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector carries an R150 approval marking unless it is replaced by a UI.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall include the four- to six-digit sequential number that is part of the approval number.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the 4- to 6-digit sequential number matching the approval.
candidates.applies_because: This is part of the required approval marking content for the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The sequential number of the approval number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
candidates.test_case: Visually check that the sequential number is located next to the circled E.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the placement rule for the approval marking of the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall include the symbol identifying the retro-reflective device ("IA" or "IB") as prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the class symbol IA or IB.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is Class IA or IB.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval (e.g. "150R01").
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for "150R" followed by the series digits.
candidates.applies_because: This is part of the required approval marking content for the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The approval marking may be replaced by the Unique Identifier, if available, in which case the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format shown in Figure I.
candidates.test_case: If a UI is used, compare the marked UI with the Figure I format.
candidates.applies_because: This is a marking option available to the retro-reflector of the rear lamp.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the sample for the applicant's trade name or mark.
candidates.applies_because: This marking applies to all retro-reflective devices.

candidates.text: The Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
candidates.test_case: Check whether the optics are orientation-dependent; if so, inspect for a horizontal "TOP" on the highest part of the illuminating surface.
candidates.applies_because: This applies to Class IA/IB retro-reflectors whose prism optics are not rotationally unambiguous.

candidates.text: The approval marking or the Unique Identifier, and the markings of paragraph 3.3.4., shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the marking legibility on the assembled lamp.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the location and legibility rule for the retro-reflector's markings.

candidates.text: Where the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps comply with several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four- to six-digit sequential number or a Unique Identifier may be affixed anywhere on the lamp assembly.
candidates.test_case: Inspect that the single approval mark covers all approvals (R148 and R150 symbols).
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is combined with R148 rear position, stop and reversing lamps in one unit.

candidates.text: In case a single approval mark is used on the combined lamp, the marking shall be visible after installation of the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Check the visibility of the marking with the lamp installed on the vehicle or in a representative fixture.
candidates.applies_because: This is a condition for single marking of the combined rear lamp.

candidates.text: In case a single approval mark is used on the combined lamp, no light-transmitting part of the lamp shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
candidates.test_case: Review the design to confirm the mark is on a light-transmitting part (e.g. the outer lens) that cannot be separated from the other transmitting parts.
candidates.applies_because: This is a condition for single marking of the combined rear lamp.

candidates.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
candidates.test_case: Measure the mark component sizes against the minimum sizes required by R148 and R150.
candidates.applies_because: This applies when the combined lamp uses a single R148/R150 approval mark.

candidates.text: Retro-reflectors approved under this Regulation shall be manufactured so as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5.
candidates.test_case: Perform periodic production tests of photometry, colorimetry and water penetration per Annex 2.
candidates.applies_because: This is the conformity of production obligation for the series-produced retro-reflector.

candidates.text: For a production retro-reflector chosen at random, no measured photometric value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI values of random production samples and compare them with 80 % of the Table 3 minima.
candidates.applies_because: This is the photometric deviation limit for production retro-reflectors, referenced by 3.5.1.1.

candidates.text: Production retro-reflectors shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates (red night-time colour).
candidates.test_case: Measure the trichromatic coordinates of production samples under Illuminant A.
candidates.applies_because: This is the colorimetric conformity of production limit for the red retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The requirements in sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications', and in the Annexes they reference, of UN Regulation No. 48 (series of amendments in force at the time of application) that are pertinent to the red rear retro-reflector and to vehicle category M1 shall be met, where their verification at the time of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
candidates.test_case: Review the R48 general and individual specifications for rear retro-reflectors on M1 vehicles and check the device for the items that can be verified at device level.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is intended for installation on M1 vehicles governed by R48.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
candidates.test_case: Confirm that the retro-reflector meets its photometric requirements before and after the prescribed resistance tests.
candidates.applies_because: This is a general construction requirement for all retro-reflective devices, including the integral retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector must not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the samples for design or manufacturing defects such as voids, sink marks or damaged prisms.
candidates.applies_because: This is a general construction requirement for all retro-reflective devices.

candidates.text: The components of the retro-reflector, or parts thereof, shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
candidates.test_case: Attempt to dismantle the retro-reflector components by hand without tools and confirm they cannot easily be separated.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector insert is mounted in the lamp assembly and must not be easy to remove.

candidates.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall be easy to clean.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the outer surface and confirm by a cleaning trial that it can be cleaned easily.
candidates.applies_because: The outer surface of the integral retro-reflector, or the lens covering it, is exposed in normal use.

candidates.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not be rough, and any protuberances it may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
candidates.test_case: Visually and tactilely inspect the outer surface for roughness and for protuberances that hinder cleaning.
candidates.applies_because: This applies to the exposed outer surface of the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector when in normal use.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the assembled lamp and confirm that the inner prism surface cannot be reached without dismantling.
candidates.applies_because: The prism (inner) surface of the retro-reflector must be enclosed in the lamp.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter (e.g. a colourless optical unit behind the red outer lens acting as filter), the optical unit and filter shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
candidates.test_case: Check by inspection and handling of the assembly that the optical unit and the filter cannot be separated in normal use.
candidates.applies_because: The open option allows a colourless optical unit behind the red outer lens acting as filter.

candidates.text: The retro-reflecting optical unit and any filter shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the material, check the drawings and examine a cross-section to confirm that the red colour is integral to the material and not a paint or varnish layer.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is red, so its colour must come from the material and not from a coating.

candidates.text: When the retro-reflector is illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° if 0° produces a colourless surface reflection), the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity shall be within the limits for the night-time colour red of retro-reflected light defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of the retro-reflected light with a colorimeter under Illuminant A at the specified geometry and compare them with the R48 red boundaries.
candidates.applies_because: The rear retro-reflector is red and must meet the night-time red chromaticity limits.

candidates.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the shape and dimension requirements of Annex 5.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the retro-reflector shape and dimensions against Annex 5, paragraph 1.
candidates.applies_because: The integral red non-triangular retro-reflector (P-05) is approved as Class IA or IB.

candidates.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements of paragraphs 5.1.4 to 5.1.5.
candidates.test_case: Perform the RI photometry and night-time colorimetry on the test samples.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements of paragraph 5.1.7 that apply to the nature of its materials and construction.
candidates.test_case: Run the heat, water, fuel/oil, corrosion, rear-face, stability and weathering tests that apply, in the prescribed order.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a moulded PMMA Class IA/IB retro-reflector subject to the resistance tests.

candidates.text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of a Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for trailer retro-reflectors when observed from a distance of 10 m.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the illuminating surface from 10 m to confirm it is not mistakable for a triangle.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a non-triangular Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The moulded plastics Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall withstand being kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, followed by cooling for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
candidates.test_case: Expose the samples in a dry oven at 65 °C for 48 h, then condition them at 23 °C for 1 h.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a moulded PMMA reflector of Class IA/IB.

candidates.text: After the heat resistance test, the retro-reflector, and in particular its optical component, shall show no visible cracking or appreciable distortion.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the samples for cracks and distortion after the heat test.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the heat test for P-05.

candidates.text: At least one hour after the heat resistance test, the retro-reflector shall meet the colorimetric requirements of 5.1.5 and the RI of 5.1.4 at a divergence angle of 20' and β1 = β2 = 0° (or the position defined in Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2). The samples with the minimum and maximum RI shall meet the complete photometry of 5.1.4.
candidates.test_case: Measure colour and RI at 20'/0° on all samples, then run complete photometry on the min and max samples.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 must keep its performance after heat exposure.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector, whether part of a lamp or not and stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand immersion for 10 min in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the top of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface. It shall also withstand a repeat with the device turned through 180° (rear face covered by about 20 mm of water), followed immediately by immersion under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.
candidates.test_case: Immerse the lamp/retro-reflector in 50 °C water in normal and inverted positions, then in 25 °C water.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a retro-reflector within the lamp and is subject to the water penetration test.

candidates.text: After the water penetration test, no water shall have penetrated to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit; visible presence of water means failure.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the reflecting surface for water; in case of doubt, re-measure the RI per 5.1.3.2.2.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the water penetration test for P-05 (Class IA, and Class IB unless the alternative applies).

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, it shall be subjected to the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6 and shall afterwards meet the colour and RI requirements of 5.1.3.2.
candidates.test_case: Run the salt-spray corrosion test, then check colour and RI at 20'/0°.
candidates.applies_because: The product inputs leave open whether metal components are present; the corrosion test then binds P-05.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector is mirror-backed with an accessible rear face, it shall be subjected to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face in Part 5 of Annex 6 and shall afterwards meet the colour and RI requirements of 5.1.3.2.
candidates.test_case: Brush the rear face with the fuel/oil mixture per Annex 6 Part 5, then measure RI and colour.
candidates.applies_because: The product inputs leave open whether the rear face is mirror-backed.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7) after a satisfactory water penetration test, and shall afterwards meet the colour and RI requirements of 5.1.3.2.
candidates.test_case: Expose the samples to the n-heptane/toluol mixture and to lubricating oil per Annex 7, then check colour and RI.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a moulded plastics Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties (Part 3 of Annex 4) and shall meet the colour and RI requirements of 5.1.3.2.
candidates.test_case: Assess the stability-in-time samples, then measure colour and RI at 20'/0°.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is subject to the third-group test for Class IA/IB.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6) and shall afterwards meet the colour and RI requirements of 5.1.3.2.
candidates.test_case: Expose the samples to accelerated weathering per EN ISO 4892-2, then check colour and RI.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is subject to the fourth-group test for Class IA/IB.

candidates.text: After undergoing the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1, the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a colour which satisfies the conditions of paragraph 5.1.5.
candidates.test_case: Measure the night-time trichromatic coordinates after each test group (visual check; coordinates in case of doubt).
candidates.applies_because: This is the post-test colour criterion for P-05.

candidates.text: After undergoing the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1, the retro-reflectors in each group shall have an RI satisfying paragraph 5.1.4, verified at a divergence angle of 20' and β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions of Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2.
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0° after each test group and compare with Table 3 (red: 300 mcd/lx).
candidates.applies_because: This is the post-test photometric criterion for P-05.

candidates.text: Where more than one axis of reference, or a range of axes, is specified by the manufacturer, the retro-reflector shall meet the RI requirements with respect to each specified axis of reference or to the extreme axes of the range.
candidates.test_case: Repeat the photometric measurements for each declared reference axis or extreme of the range.
candidates.applies_because: The RI limits of P-05 apply for each declared axis of reference.

candidates.text: For photometric measurements of the Class IA/IB retro-reflector, only the illuminating surface contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered. This surface is defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system as indicated by the manufacturer.
candidates.test_case: Check on the drawing and sample that the declared illuminating surface lies within a 200 mm diameter circle.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the area of P-05 that counts for photometry.

candidates.text: The illuminating surface considered for photometry shall be limited to 100 cm², though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not attain this area.
candidates.test_case: Measure the declared illuminating surface area and confirm it is not more than 100 cm².
candidates.applies_because: This sets the photometric area limit for P-05.

candidates.text: The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the illuminating surface area to be used for photometric measurement of the retro-reflector.
candidates.test_case: Check the approval documentation for the declared perimeter of the illuminating surface.
candidates.applies_because: The design documentation of P-05 must define the measured area.

candidates.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall be equal to or greater than those of Table 3, in mcd/lx, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
candidates.test_case: Perform goniophotometric RI measurement per Annex 4 Part 1 and compare with Table 3.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a red Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The minimum RI values for a red Class IA/IB retro-reflector are as follows. At divergence angle 20': 300 mcd/lx at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, 200 mcd/lx at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0° and 100 mcd/lx at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°. At divergence angle 1°30': 5 mcd/lx at 0°/0°, 2.8 mcd/lx at ±10°/0° and 2.5 mcd/lx at ±5°/±20°.
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI at each listed divergence/illumination angle combination and compare with the minima.
candidates.applies_because: These are the Table 3 values for the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector P-05.

candidates.text: Within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°), the RI values of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall not be lower than the Table 3 values at the boundary of that solid angle (100 mcd/lx at 20' and 2.5 mcd/lx at 1°30').
candidates.test_case: Scan the RI within the bounded solid angle at both divergence angles and confirm no value falls below the limit.
candidates.applies_because: This RI floor within the solid angle applies to the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector P-05.

candidates.text: In case the Class IA/IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values may be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
candidates.test_case: Confirm the declared mounting height; if it is below 750 mm, verify the downward RI only to 5°.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp of the M1 vehicle may be mounted below 750 mm, which reduces the photometric field of P-05.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector is not marked "TOP", its RI at β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5) and a divergence of 20', measured in the rotational position about the axis of reference giving minimum RI, shall conform to paragraph 5. The device may be rotated ±5° from that position if the specified values for the other angles are not attained.
candidates.test_case: Rotate the sample about its reference axis to the minimum-RI position and measure the RI at all required angles.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 may not carry a TOP marking, so its orientation-dependent RI must still comply.

candidates.text: When tested according to paragraph 4.2.1 (CIE Standard Illuminant A, divergence 1/3°, β1 = β2 = 0°), the trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colour red specified in UN Regulation No. 48. This applies whether the colour comes from a red optical unit or from a colourless unit behind the red outer lens acting as filter.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of the retro-reflected light with a spectroradiometer under Illuminant A and check it against the R48 red night-time boundaries.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a red rear retro-reflector.

candidates.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors (Class IA/IB, red) shall conform to the approved type from a mechanical and geometric standpoint, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Dimensionally inspect production retro-reflectors against the approved type drawings and the Annex 5 Class IA/IB shape and dimension requirements.
candidates.applies_because: The integral red retro-reflector is R150-approved and must be produced in conformity with the approved type.

candidates.text: When the photometric performance of any production retro-reflector chosen at random is tested, no measured value of the coefficient of luminous intensity (CIL) shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Measure the CIL of randomly selected production retro-reflectors at the prescribed angles and check that every value is at least 80 per cent of the prescribed minimum.
candidates.applies_because: This limits how far the photometric performance of production retro-reflectors may deviate.

candidates.text: Production retro-reflectors shall comply with the prescribed chromaticity coordinates for red.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of randomly selected production retro-reflectors and verify they lie within the red boundaries of the Regulation.
candidates.applies_because: The red retro-reflector must keep its colour within the red limits in series production.

candidates.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors shall conform to the approved type from a mechanical and geometric standpoint: differences shall not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.
candidates.test_case: Compare the dimensions and geometry of randomly chosen production retro-reflectors against the approved drawings and the approval sample.
candidates.applies_because: The R150 retro-reflector (P-05) built into the rear lamp is mass-produced under the approval and is subject to conformity of production.

candidates.text: When the photometric performance of any mass-produced retro-reflector chosen at random is tested, no measured value of the coefficient of luminous intensity (CIL) shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Measure the CIL of randomly selected production retro-reflectors at the prescribed angles and check each value is at least 80 % of the prescribed minimum.
candidates.applies_because: The production Class IA/IB red retro-reflector must keep its CIL within the permitted CoP deviation.

candidates.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates prescribed for red.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of production retro-reflectors under the prescribed colorimetric conditions and check they lie within the red boundaries.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector of the rear lamp is red, either as a red optical unit or behind the red outer lens acting as filter, and production units must stay within the red colour limits.

candidates.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors shall pass the resistance to water penetration test of Annex 6, Part 2, paragraph 1: no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
candidates.test_case: Immerse a production retro-reflector (part of the lamp) per Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1. Inspect for water at the reflecting surface and, in case of doubt, measure the CIL.
candidates.applies_because: Conformity of production of the retro-reflector in the rear lamp includes the water penetration test on production samples.

candidates.text: If a mirror effect is produced when the RI of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector is measured at an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (checked by slightly turning the device), the RI reading shall be taken at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.
candidates.test_case: Turn the retro-reflector slightly at β1 = β2 = 0° on the goniometer to check for a mirror effect; if present, measure RI at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° and compare with Table 3.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the illumination angle at which the RI of the integral red retro-reflector is assessed for compliance.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector is not marked "TOP", its RI at the position of minimum RI, found by rotating it about its axis of reference at β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5) and a divergence angle of 20', shall conform to the value specified in paragraph 5 (red Class IA/IB: ≥ 300 mcd/lx).
candidates.test_case: Rotate the unmarked retro-reflector through 360° about its reference axis at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, find the minimum RI and check it is ≥ 300 mcd/lx.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector must meet the minimum RI in its worst rotational position if it carries no TOP marking.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector is not marked "TOP", the RI at the other illumination and divergence angles shall be met with the device in the rotational position ε of minimum RI; if the specified values are not attained there, the device may be rotated about its axis of reference by ±5° from that position.
candidates.test_case: Perform complete photometry at the ε of minimum RI; where a value fails, re-measure within ±5° of that ε and check compliance with Table 3.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the rotational position, and the permitted ±5° tolerance, in which the full Table 3 photometry of the unmarked retro-reflector must be met.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector is marked "TOP", its RI shall not fall below the prescribed value in any position reached while it is rotated about its axis by ±5° at β1 = β2 = 0° (or the specified angle) and a divergence angle of 20'.
candidates.test_case: Rotate the TOP-marked retro-reflector ±5° about its reference axis at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, record RI continuously and check it never falls below 300 mcd/lx.
candidates.applies_because: A TOP-marked integral retro-reflector must keep the minimum RI over a ±5° rotation tolerance.

candidates.text: If the RI of the retro-reflector at β1 = β2 = 0° and ε = 0° exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, compliance at all angles of illumination and divergence shall be assessed at ε = 0°.
candidates.test_case: Measure RI at ε = 0°, β1 = β2 = 0° and 20'; if ≥ 150 % of the requirement, perform all Table 3 measurements at ε = 0°.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the rotational position in which the retro-reflector's full photometric compliance is judged when on-axis performance is high.

candidates.text: The retro-reflection (RI) of the retro-reflector shall be assessed with the device illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the photometric test report states Illuminant A source conditions for all RI measurements of the retro-reflector.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the illuminant under which the red retro-reflector must achieve its RI values.

candidates.text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of the Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for retro-reflectors of Classes IIIA/IIIB (trailers) when viewed from an observation distance of 10 metres.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the retro-reflector illuminating surface from 10 m and confirm its shape cannot be easily confused with a triangle.
candidates.applies_because: The integral non-triangular red retro-reflector of the rear lamp is approved as Class IA or IB.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector, whether part of a lamp or not and stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand immersion for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface. The immersion is repeated after turning the device through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water. The device is then immediately immersed under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C. This applies to Class IA, and to Class IB unless the alternative moisture and dust test is applied.
candidates.test_case: Immerse the stripped retro-reflector (or lamp assembly) at 50 °C for 10 min in each orientation, then at 25 °C, as prescribed.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's integral red retro-reflector (P-05) is a Class IA/IB retro-reflector that must pass the water penetration test.

candidates.text: After the water immersion test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit. If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the retro-reflector shall not be considered to have passed the test.
candidates.test_case: After immersion, visually inspect the prism reflecting surface for any water ingress.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the water penetration test for the Class IA/IB retro-reflector of the lamp.

candidates.text: If visual inspection after the water immersion test does not reveal water, or in case of doubt, the retro-reflector's coefficient of luminous intensity (RI) shall still satisfy the conditions of paragraph 5.1.4. The device is first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside. RI is measured per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0°, or if necessary in all positions of Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2.
candidates.test_case: Shake off excess water and measure RI at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0° on the goniometer; compare with the paragraph 5.1.4 limits.
candidates.applies_because: This is the photometric pass criterion after the water test for the lamp's retro-reflector.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB (lamp not watertight) where the moisture and dust tests are applied as the alternative to the water penetration test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open during the water spray test, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the test sample to confirm drain holes and openings are unobstructed and drain wicks are fitted as in production.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector may be Class IB in a non-watertight rear lamp, and the moisture test is then an option for it.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the moisture test applied, the device shall be exposed to a solid cone water spray at a precipitation rate of 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min, directed downward at 45° ± 5°, while rotating about its vertical axis at 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.
candidates.test_case: Run the water spray cabinet test with the calibrated precipitation rate and rotation speed and record the parameters.
candidates.applies_because: This is the water exposure the Class IB retro-reflector, grouped in the rear lamp, must withstand.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the moisture test applied, because the retro-reflector is grouped or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position, stop and reversing lamps, these functions shall be operated at design voltage during the water spray in a cycle of 5 min ON and 55 min OFF.
candidates.test_case: Energise the lamp functions at design voltage with a 5/55 min timer during the spray test and log the cycles.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is integrated into a rear combination lamp with signalling and lighting functions.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the moisture test applied, the water spray exposure shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min), followed by a 1 hour drain period with rotation and spray turned off and the cabinet door closed.
candidates.test_case: Verify the test log shows 12 h of spray exposure followed by 1 h of draining.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the duration of the moisture stress on the Class IB retro-reflector device.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the moisture test applied, after the drain period no standing pool of water shall have formed in the interior of the device, nor shall one be formable by tapping or tilting the device.
candidates.test_case: After draining, inspect the interior visually, tap and tilt the lamp, and check for pooled water.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion for moisture penetration of the Class IB lamp containing the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the moisture test applied, after the water spray test and with the exterior dried, the RI of the retro-reflector measured according to Part 1 of Annex 4 shall satisfy the conditions of paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 (divergence 20', illumination β1 = β2 = 0°).
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI on a goniophotometer at 20' divergence and 0° illumination after the test and compare it with the required value.
candidates.applies_because: The photometric performance of the retro-reflector must be retained after moisture exposure.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the dust test applied, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open during the dust exposure, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the sample before dust exposure to confirm openings are open and wicks are installed.
candidates.applies_because: The dust test is the companion test to the moisture alternative for a Class IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the dust test applied, the device shall be exposed for 5 hours in a dust chamber charged with 3 to 5 kg of fine powdered cement to ASTM C 150-84, with the dust agitated every 15 min for 2 to 15 s and allowed to settle between agitations.
candidates.test_case: Perform the dust chamber exposure with the specified dust, charge and agitation cycle, and record the parameters.
candidates.applies_because: This is the dust exposure the Class IB retro-reflector device must withstand.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the dust test applied, after the dust exposure and with the exterior cleaned and dried, the RI of the retro-reflector measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 shall satisfy the conditions of paragraph 5.1.4.
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI at 20' divergence and 0° illumination after the dust test and compare it with the required value.
candidates.applies_because: Dust penetration must not significantly affect the photometric output of the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector (Class IA/IB) shall be designed so that it retains the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which it is normally exposed.
candidates.test_case: Perform the ISO 9227:2017 salt-mist corrosion test, then re-measure photometric and colorimetric values against the R150 limits.
candidates.applies_because: The integral red retro-reflector P-05 is a retro-reflective device approved under R150 and is exposed to humidity and road salt at the vehicle rear.

candidates.text: The front surface of the retro-reflector shall resist tarnishing, and the protection of its rear face shall resist deterioration, when tested for corrosion according to ISO 9227:2017, particularly where an essential metal component is liable to be attacked.
candidates.test_case: After the ISO 9227:2017 salt-mist exposure, visually inspect the front surface for tarnishing and the rear-face protection for deterioration.
candidates.applies_because: The corrosion resistance check covers the front surface and rear-face protection of the retro-reflector P-05, including any metallised rear face.

candidates.text: Because the retro-reflector is combined with a light, the complete lamp, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand a saline mist for 50 hours, comprising two 24-hour exposure periods separated by a 2-hour interval in which the sample is allowed to dry.
candidates.test_case: Expose the stripped rear lamp in a salt-spray chamber for 2 × 24 h with a 2 h drying interval between them, then evaluate it.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is integrated in the rear combination lamp, so the lamp itself is the corrosion test sample.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion (e.g. a metallised mirror-backed rear face), the saline mist shall be produced by atomizing, at 35 °C ± 2 °C, a solution of 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent impurities.
candidates.test_case: Verify the salt-spray chamber settings (35 ± 2 °C, 5 % NaCl solution in distilled water) in the test report for a retro-reflector with metal components.
candidates.applies_because: Whether the retro-reflector has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion (e.g. a metallised mirror-backed rear face) is an open option for this product.

candidates.text: Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the retro-reflector sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the sample immediately after the salt-mist exposure for corrosion that could impair retro-reflective efficiency.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the corrosion test that binds the R150 retro-reflector P-05.

candidates.text: After a recovery period of 48 hours following the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, measured as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6 at an entrance angle β2 = 5° and an observation angle α = 20', shall be not less than the minimum value of the referenced Table 9 and not more than the maximum value of the referenced Table 10.
candidates.test_case: After 48 h recovery and removal of salt deposits, measure RA at β2 = 5° and α = 20' and compare the result with the referenced limits.
candidates.applies_because: This photometric pass criterion after the corrosion test applies to the retro-reflective areas of the device under test.

candidates.text: In case of a mirror-backed retro-reflector (Class IA or IB moulded plastics) with an accessible rear face, the rear face shall withstand, after being brushed with a hard nylon brush, the application for one minute of a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol (Annex 7 Part 1), followed by drying and brushing again with the same brush.
candidates.test_case: Brush the rear face, apply a cotton cloth soaked in 70/30 n-heptane/toluol for 1 min, let dry, brush again, then inspect and proceed to the RI measurement.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is a Class IA/IB moulded plastics device and the mirror-backed rear face is an open option.

candidates.text: In case of a mirror-backed retro-reflector (Class IA or IB) with an accessible rear face, after the rear-face solvent and brushing test and with the whole mirror-backed rear face covered with Indian ink, the coefficient of luminous intensity (RI) shall still satisfy the conditions of paragraph 5.1.4, verified at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2).
candidates.test_case: Cover the whole tested rear face with Indian ink and measure RI at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0°, then compare the result with the paragraph 5.1.4 limits for red Class IA/IB.
candidates.applies_because: The pass criterion of the rear-face resistance test applies to a mirror-backed Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector, in particular its illuminating surface, shall withstand exposure to a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol, applied by lightly wiping with a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture.
candidates.test_case: Lightly wipe the outer and illuminating surface of the retro-reflector with a cotton cloth soaked in 70/30 n-heptane/toluol.
candidates.applies_because: The Class IA/IB retro-reflector of the rear lamp must pass the fuel resistance test of Annex 7 Part 1.

candidates.text: About five minutes after wiping with the n-heptane/toluol test mixture, the outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks are not objected to.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the wiped surface about 5 minutes after application for surface changes other than slight cracks.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the fuel resistance test for retro-reflective devices, which covers the integral retro-reflector.

candidates.text: After its outer surface, in particular the illuminating surface, has been exposed for about 5 minutes to a detergent lubricating oil (lightly applied with a soaked cotton cloth) and then cleaned, the Class IA/IB moulded plastics retro-reflector shall have a coefficient of luminous intensity (CIL) that still meets paragraph 5.1.4. This is checked at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0°, or if necessary in all positions specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2.
candidates.test_case: Wipe the outer and illuminating surface with detergent lubricating oil, wait 5 min and clean it, then measure the CIL at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0° and compare with the paragraph 5.1.4 limits.
candidates.applies_because: The red PMMA moulded prism retro-reflector of the rear lamp is a Class IA/IB moulded plastics retro-reflector covered by this lubricating-oil resistance test.

candidates.text: The approval number (sequential number) on the retro-reflector's approval marking must be placed close to the circle surrounding the letter "E", in any position relative to it.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the marking on the retro-reflector or lamp and check that the approval number is adjacent to the E-circle.
candidates.applies_because: The Class IA/IB retro-reflector of the rear lamp carries an R150 approval marking.

candidates.text: The digits making up the approval number on the retro-reflector's approval marking must face the same way as the letter "E".
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the marking and check that the approval-number digits have the same orientation as the "E".
candidates.applies_because: The R150 approval marking applies to the integral retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The group of symbols indicating the class of the retro-reflector (IA or IB) must be placed diametrically opposite the approval number with respect to the E-circle.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the marking and check that the class symbol (IA/IB) sits on the opposite side of the E-circle from the approval number.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is approved as Class IA or IB, and its class symbol forms part of the marking.

candidates.text: The external projection provisions do not apply to those parts of the rear lamp's external surface (outer lens, exposed housing/bezel, exposed seal) which, with the vehicle laden and all doors, windows and access lids closed, are at a height of more than 2 metres.
candidates.test_case: Measure the height of the installed lamp's exposed surfaces above ground with the vehicle in laden condition.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's exposed surfaces are part of the M1 vehicle external surface; this exemption limits which zones must comply.

candidates.text: The external projection provisions do not apply to those parts of the rear lamp's external surface which, with the vehicle laden and all doors, windows and access lids closed, are below the floor line.
candidates.test_case: Determine the floor line on the laden vehicle and check the position of the lamp surfaces relative to it.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp forms part of the vehicle external surface, and this exemption defines zones outside the requirements.

candidates.text: In case the lamp is recessed or overhung by the body, the external projection provisions do not apply to those parts of the rear lamp's external surface which, in their static condition and in operation, cannot be contacted by a sphere 100 mm in diameter (vehicle laden, all doors, windows and access lids closed).
candidates.test_case: Pass a 100 mm diameter sphere over the installed lamp area and identify the surfaces it cannot contact.
candidates.applies_because: A lamp that is flush or recessed in the body panel may have edges a 100 mm sphere cannot reach, and those edges are then exempt.

candidates.text: The external surface of the installed rear lamp (outer lens, exposed housing/bezel and any exposed seal) shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by or brushing against it in a collision.
candidates.test_case: Visually and tactilely inspect the installed lamp for outward-directed pointed, sharp or injurious projections.
candidates.applies_because: Para 2.3 makes lighting and light-signalling devices part of the M1 vehicle external surface.

candidates.text: The external surface of the installed rear lamp shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the installed lamp contour for hooks, open edges or gaps that could catch clothing or limbs.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's exposed lens and bezel form part of the vehicle external surface.

candidates.text: No protruding part of the rear lamp's external surface (lens edges, housing/bezel rim) shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm, except that this does not apply to parts protruding less than 5 mm.
candidates.test_case: Measure the projection per Annex 3 para 2 and gauge the radii of the exposed edges with radius gauges.
candidates.applies_because: In case the lamp protrudes beyond the panel nominal line, its exposed edges are protruding parts of the external surface.

candidates.text: Where parts of the rear lamp's external surface protrude less than 5 mm (but 1.5 mm or more), their outward facing angles shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.
candidates.test_case: Measure the projection height of the edge relative to the panel and inspect the outward facing angles for blunting.
candidates.applies_because: In case some exposed lens or bezel edges have radii below 2.5 mm, this applies through the low-projection exemption.

candidates.text: Protruding parts of the rear lamp's external surface made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A (e.g. an exposed TPE/silicone seal) may have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm.
candidates.test_case: Measure the Shore A hardness of the exposed seal with it installed on the vehicle and confirm it is 60 Shore A or less.
candidates.applies_because: In case the gasket is visible at the external surface, its soft material may make use of this relaxation.

candidates.text: For the Shore A hardness relaxation, the hardness of the rear lamp part shall be determined with the component as installed on the vehicle, using comparable measurements where a Shore A measurement is impossible.
candidates.test_case: Perform a Shore A durometer measurement on the seal in its installed position on the vehicle.
candidates.applies_because: The hardness relaxation for an exposed seal depends on hardness measured as installed.

candidates.text: Series-production rear lamps fitted to the approved M1 vehicle type shall conform to the approved type by meeting the external-projection requirements of paragraphs 5 and 6. This covers the exposed outer lens, any visible housing rim or bezel and any exposed seal, which must have no pointed or sharp outward parts, no catching parts, a radius of curvature of at least 2.5 mm, or the permitted protrusion- or hardness-based exemptions.
candidates.test_case: On production samples taken at random, measure edge radii and projection heights of the installed lamp per Annex 3 and Shore A hardness of any exposed soft parts, and compare with the approved type.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's exposed surfaces form part of the M1 vehicle's external surface under R26, and production parts must keep the approved external-projection compliance.

candidates.text: In case the rear lamp protrudes beyond the panel nominal line and is mounted on a convex surface, the dimension of the projection of the lamp may be determined either directly or by reference to a drawing of an appropriate section of the lamp in its installed condition.
candidates.test_case: Measure the lamp's projection directly on the vehicle, or check it on the manufacturer's section drawing of the installed lamp.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is a component mounted on the M1 external surface, and the size of its projection must be determined to check it against the paragraph 5 and 6 limits.

candidates.text: In case the rear lamp protrudes beyond the panel nominal line and is mounted on a surface other than convex, and its projection cannot be determined by simple measurement, the dimension of the projection of the lamp shall be determined as the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal line of the panel when the sphere is moved over the lamp in constant contact with it.
candidates.test_case: Move a 100 mm diameter sphere over the installed lamp in constant contact and record the maximum variation of its centre from the panel nominal line.
candidates.applies_because: This defines how the projection of the installed lamp is measured where it sits on a non-convex body panel.

candidates.text: The rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamps and rear retro-reflector) shall be so fitted that, under normal conditions of use and notwithstanding any vibrations to which it may be subjected, it retains the characteristics prescribed by UN R48 and enables the vehicle to comply with UN R48.
candidates.test_case: Vibration test of the lamp on its vehicle mounting, then re-check position, orientation and photometry.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is a lighting and light-signalling device fitted on an M1 vehicle.

candidates.text: It shall not be possible for the rear combination lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the mounting design and check orientation after handling and vibration loading.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's fasteners and clips must hold its aim on the vehicle.

candidates.text: When fitted to the vehicle, the reference axis of each light-signalling function of the rear lamp (rear position, stop, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector) shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.
candidates.test_case: Measure the vertical angle of the lamp reference axis relative to the ground plane on the installed lamp.
candidates.applies_because: All light-signalling devices of the lamp are subject to this orientation rule.

candidates.text: When fitted to the vehicle, the reference axis of each light-signalling function of the rear lamp shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
candidates.test_case: Measure the horizontal angle of the lamp reference axis relative to the vehicle median longitudinal plane.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp functions are signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors or side-marker lamps.

candidates.text: Any specific fitting instructions laid down by the lamp manufacturer shall be complied with when the rear lamp is installed.
candidates.test_case: Compare the installation against the manufacturer's fitting instructions.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp manufacturer's fitting instructions bind its installation.

candidates.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the rear lamp shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and on a flat, horizontal surface, in normal condition of use.
candidates.test_case: Measure height and orientation with the vehicle unladen on a flat horizontal surface.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the vehicle condition in which the lamp's height and orientation must comply.

candidates.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the left and right rear lamps forming a pair shall be fitted symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane, based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface.
candidates.test_case: Measure lateral positions of the left and right lamp outer geometry relative to the vehicle centreline.
candidates.applies_because: Rear combination lamps are fitted as a left/right pair.

candidates.text: The left and right rear lamps of a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this does not apply to the interior structure of the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Compare the exterior geometry of the left and right lamps for mirror symmetry.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is supplied as a mirrored left/right pair.

candidates.text: The left and right rear lamps of a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
